- Overestimate prices after strong sentiment spikes (positive sentiment > 0.5) — model tends to overshoot in the short term.
- Underestimate prices when sentiment is weak or negative (sentiment < 0.2) — model fails to capture downward pressure.
- Lag in price correction: model often lags 1–3 days behind true price movements, especially after sentiment shifts.
- Mean reversion bias: model overcorrects after sharp moves, leading to over- or under-forecasting in the following 5–7 days.
- Horizon-specific error: 30-day forecasts are consistently too high in early periods (first 5–7 days) when sentiment is rising, then adjust but still lag behind true peak.
- Avoid averaging sentiment across all days — weight recent sentiment (last 3–5 days) more heavily for short-term correction.
- If sentiment is trending upward, reduce forecast slope to avoid over-optimism; if trending downward, increase downward bias.
